# TrustyCodeBlock

`Data Display` · composition depth: `composite`

A multi-line code surface: a header with the language label and a copy-to-clipboard
button, above the code with a line-number gutter in a two-axis scroll area.
Setting `language` also syntax-highlights the code via Shiki (Tokyo Night theme,
loaded lazily); omit it for plain preformatted text.

Read-only by default. Set `editable` and the header gains an **Edit** button:
pressing it swaps the code for a CodeMirror editor — same grammars and theme, so
the colours don't shift — and replaces Edit with **Save**. The language label
becomes a ghost select, collapsed until clicked, so the user can switch the
grammar while editing. It opens on the `language` prop, falling back to JSON
when that is omitted. Save commits the draft, returns to the read view, and fires
`submit` with the new code and language. Bind `v-model:code` (and
`v-model:language`) to have the edit written back to your own state as well; a
plain `:code` / `:language` binding still updates what's displayed. The draft — code and
language alike — is local until Save, so an abandoned edit emits nothing.

While editing, **Tab** indents by two spaces and **Shift+Tab** outdents; **Esc then
Tab** leaves the editor, since Tab no longer moves focus. CodeMirror loads on
first edit from its own chunk, so a consumer who never sets `editable` never
ships it.

Constrain the height from outside (`max-block-size` on the component) to make
long code scroll; unconstrained, the block grows with its content.

**Use it when**
- showing a multi-line snippet the user may want to read or copy: payloads, configs, logs.
- letting the user correct that snippet in place — set `editable`.

**Don't use it for**
- a short inline reference (a file name, a property) inside running text: use a plain
  `<code>` element — the base stylesheet styles it on the design system.
- a single line of free text or an identifier in a form: use `TrustyTextInput`.
- prose in a form: use `TrustyTextInput` — the mono font and gutter are wrong for sentences.

```ts
import { TrustyCodeBlock } from '@louislp/trusty-ui'
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lineNumbers` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the line-number gutter. |
| `copyable` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the copy-to-clipboard button in the header. |
| `editable` | `boolean` | `false` | Offer an Edit button in the header, swapping the code for an editor. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `undefined` | Shown while the editor is empty (edit mode only). |
| `code` | `string` | `""` | The code, verbatim. A plain `:code` binding is enough — Save still updates what's displayed — while `v-model:code` also writes the edit back to the consumer's own state. |
| `language` | `"javascript" \| "json" \| "python" \| "typescript"` | — | Language shown in the header and used for syntax highlighting; omit for plain text. While editing, the header turns it into a picker (JSON when unset), and Save commits the pick the same way it commits the code. |

## Events

- `submit` — `[code: string, language: "javascript" \| "json" \| "python" \| "typescript"]`
- `update:code` — `[value: string]`
- `update:language` — `[value: "javascript" \| "json" \| "python" \| "typescript" \| undefined]`

## Examples in Storybook

- Default — Default — header with language + copy button, line numbers on.
- ConstrainedHeight — Height constrained from outside: the content scrolls vertically.
- HorizontalScroll — Long lines scroll horizontally; the gutter stays pinned.
- Python — Other supported languages.
- TypeScript
- PlainText — No language: plain preformatted text, no highlighting.
- NoLineNumbers
- NotCopyable
- Editable — `editable`: the header offers Edit, which swaps the code for the editor.
- Editing — Edit mode, opened by the play function: the language label is now a ghost select, collapsed until the user opens it. Picking a language re-highlights the editor at once; Save commits it.
- EditableWithBinding — `v-model:code` writes the saved edit back into the consumer's own state.
- WideContainer — The parent owns the width. The same code that scrolls horizontally in the 320px stories above fits without scrolling here — the component fills what it's given and never sets a width of its own, in either mode.
